content.text:
Rewrote `/private/tmp/gndfv/0.svg`. The original was a single empty root element with no size, no coordinate system, no accessible name, and no content, so it rendered as nothing. I did not add artwork, because nothing in the file or directory indicates what it is supposed to depict.

The file now reads:

```svg
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="100" height="100" role="img">
  <title>Untitled</title>
  <!-- Add graphic content here. The coordinate system is 100 x 100 units. -->
</svg>
```

What changed:

- **Intrinsic size and coordinate system.** The viewBox plus width and height give it a defined 100 by 100 canvas, so it scales predictably instead of falling back to the browser default of 300 by 150.
- **Accessibility.** The image role and a title element give screen readers something to announce. Rename "Untitled" once you know what the graphic is.
- **Standalone-file hygiene.** An XML declaration with UTF-8 encoding, an explicit open and close tag so content can be added, and a trailing newline.
- **A placeholder comment** marking where shapes go. Delete it when you add content.
